correctness.rationale: The exact coin minimum recurrence and 16-shift induction give the Apéry formula for a>=34. The generator-by-generator PF inequalities reduce all cases to two low residues and 256 exact terminal comparisons. Every terminal wrap inequality is proved at a representative a=34..49 and transfers monotonically. All rejected cases have a persistent nonwrap witness. Dijkstra and direct gap tests corroborate. Exact failure at a=33 is explicitly exhibited.

evidence: Bogart–Goodrick–Woods establish eventual quasi-polynomial type for arbitrary polynomial generator families, but no explicit period or sharp threshold here.

Stamate–Strazzanti establish an eventual bijection for pseudo-Frobenius elements of shifted families and use sufficient n>r_k^2 (which is n>256 for r_k=16); their theorem does not enumerate the present values nor cover the threshold 34.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These are genuine broader qualitative periodicity theorems. They do not make the exact K_q table or the 33-to-34 threshold an immediately stated specialization; using them would still require new substantive residue and boundary computations.

value.rationale: The complete PF spectrum and type are fundamental invariants of a naturally studied five-generator square-offset semigroup family. It sharpens the known Frobenius-only classification into 16 exact full spectra, a least-period type law, and a demonstrably sharp onset a=34. Type 6..9 exceeds its five minimal generators, exhibiting nontrivial socle behavior. Results are not mere enumerated cases.
